designSystemPrimitives.why: The two-step arm-then-confirm destructive control (4 callers). `library.html:570` specifies `danger` as one of six ROLES on the single button primitive and `library.html:1815` records a bespoke destructive panel as a surface Foundry already owns, so the arm is a carve-out neither entry claims by name.

The shared bulk-DELETE card (3 callers, issue 1132). `library.html:1058` specifies `<SelectionBar>` and `<BulkEditPanel>` for this surface and names no delete card. Targeted because it renders in all three studios but is photographed only by the four `*-bulk-delete-*` frames, which `ui-pr-screenshot-evidence.mjs` routes it to; the bulk-EDIT frames do not contain it.

The bulk panel shell (3 callers, issue 1010). `library.html:1058` names it and calls this "the largest uncovered surface in the corpus". Targeted: exactly two studios consume it and both claim it by `sourceMatches`.
A section inside the bulk panel (3 callers, issue 1010). `library.html:1058` specifies the PANEL, not its internal sectioning. Targeted for the same reason as its shell.

The bulk panel's leave-unchanged select (2 callers, issue 1010). `library.html:646` specifies `<Select>` as one shell shared with text, number and search, and records the leave-unchanged clear state on `<TintPicker>` rather than on the field shell. Targeted for the same reason as its shell.
The bulk selection toolbar (3 callers, issue 1010). Named at `library.html:1058`. Targeted for the same reason as its shell.
Named at `library.html:911`. 7 callers across the manager, so no frame is a non-arbitrary choice.

The highest-traffic primitive in the codebase at 67 callers. `library.html:858` groups `<Kicker> <IconChip> <StatBox>` as the mark vocabulary and this is the icon chip. Broad by an enormous margin — attributing a chip change to one window would be a lie about where it lands.

The complication summary row (5 callers, reaching the player crafting and inventory apps as well as the component editor). `library.html:1429` names component complications among the rows `<SortableList>` "opens in place", so this row is specified as a STATE of that primitive rather than as an entry of its own. Targeted: three complication frames claim it, led by `manager-component-complications-collapsed`.

The editor tab strip. TEN importers under `src/`, which is the membership bar's own predicate, and NINE of them are wrapping strips: the system, environment, recipe-item, Checks, Knowledge, recipe, essence, tool and vocabulary strips each wrap it, while `scoped/WorldEssenceEntryPage` renders it inline without a wrapper. Both numbers are written out because this row said `8 callers` while nine files imported it — the inline caller was uncounted, and a single figure cannot say whether it means importers or wrappers. `library.html:1008` specifies `<PageHeader> <TabBar>` and states that a studio never puts its tabs in a side rail. Its specimen also draws TWO Rail Marker Family vehicles on one bar — `Tiers 3` and `Businesses 23` as bare counts beside a warning badge on Validation — so drawing the family is part of what the entry specifies, not an extension of it, and spec.md requirement "Near-neighbour primitives are routed by a stated rule" forbids substituting one vehicle for another. Issue 1038 ruled the Checks section strip OUT of conversion, led by the reason that its count "is a bare mono numeral, not a chip — the two treatments are deliberately different"; that ruling was never recorded in this manifest, and it was wrong twice over — a deliberate STYLE divergence is the one kind a shared primitive may not record, and the strip was RIGHT about the marks while the primitive was too narrow to express them. Issue 1429 made the family a capability instead, and the Checks strip is a caller as of that change. Issue 1038's OTHER three conversions stand and are counted above — the recipe, essence and tool editors — and the capabilities they needed (a chip accessible name, a chip modifier class, the `positive` tone spelling and a suppressible tab hook) live on the primitive rather than in a hand-rolled strip. Issue 1429 converted the LAST hand-rolled strip, `TagsCategoriesView`'s inlined vocabulary tablist, by extracting it as `VocabularyTabs` first — it had survived issue 1038 only because it was not a standalone component and so was never counted. Its record counts moved from the neutral chip onto the count vehicle in the same change, the same substitution the Knowledge strip carried. The one manager strip still recorded as NOT a caller is `downtime/WorldDowntimeTabs`, in {@link NOT_A_PRIMITIVE}, and that row records CONVERSION-PENDING work rather than a justified divergence — read it there before re-deriving the question. Targeted: one frame per wrapping editor claims it.

THE editor validation surface, and a CLOSED one since issue 1444 (4 direct callers, 7 renderers): every surface in the manager that draws the aggregate header over the grouped row stack goes through it, so `manager-recipe-val-*` and `manager-recipe-rail-*` have exactly one writer. `library.html` splits validation into `<ValidationList>` and `<ValidationSummary>`; this one component covers both roles, so the correspondence is still not established and is left for the conformance change to adjudicate rather than guessed at here.

Named at `library.html:911`. 43 callers, second only to `Chip`. Carries a `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry because both representative frames are POPULATED states, so the dashed panel it draws appears in neither.

The explainer card (3 callers). `library.html:911` groups `<Callout> <Notice> <InfoStrip> <Empty>` under one head and carries no prose distinguishing `<Notice>` from `<InfoStrip>`, so which of the two this card is cannot be read off the library.

The labelled icon-and-fact row (5 callers). `<StatBox>` (`library.html:858`) is the nearest mark, but a stat box is a boxed value and this is a row of label-plus-fact, so the correspondence is not made.
The inline vocabulary add field (2 callers, `VocabularyPanel.svelte` and `ImportFolderMappingModal.svelte`). No `library.html` entry names it. Targeted: `manager-tags-categories-normal` claims it.

THE right-hand inspector's action button, and the row issue 1446 finally moved. `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/essences/EssenceBrowserInspector.svelte` (issue 1036) and `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/scoped/WorldEssenceCataloguePage.svelte` (issue 1400) both import it, so it clears the two-caller bar. It sat in {@link NOT_A_PRIMITIVE} through two issues after the second adopter landed, with its own text saying it was OWED A MOVE nobody had made — which is why the change that moved it also ships the guard that re-measures a caller claim against the tree, rather than only the move. `library: null` is a judgement, and it follows `ArmedDangerButton` rather than `InspectorCard`. `library.html:570` heads its block `<Button> <IconButton>` and specifies "One component, six roles, two sizes"; `ManagerButton.svelte` claims that entry and IS that closed role set. This file's four tones — neutral, primary, danger and warning — are four of those six roles by name, and it exists precisely BECAUSE it could not be `.manager-button`: its own header records that `.fabricate-manager .manager-button.is-primary` is three classes against a scoped rule's two, so reusing the class would put the primitive's own tones behind the global sheet's. A second file claiming the entry would assert that the tree holds ONE button component where it measurably holds two. That is the `ManagerSearchField` call — `library: null` rather than claim `<Search>` and assert a shell the tree does not have — not the `InspectorCard` one, which claims `<Card>` and diverges on radius and padding, a divergence in VALUES on the file that IS the entry. The one library entry that names this surface at all rules itself out: `library.html:1243`'s inspector rail section is "Read-only by convention — it shows consequences and links out, and never hosts the editing controls", and this is the editing controls. Targeted, and its claim set is complete only as of issue 1446. The four `manager-essences-*` frames name this path in `sourceMatches`. `world-essence-catalogue` renders it too — its `essenceInspectorFoot` snippet is the `Open definition` primary, and that case asserts `[data-scoped-list-inspector-foot]` is inside the inspector — and it did NOT claim it, so a change here published four frames of one caller and none of the other. That claim is added. No `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry is owed: an override is consulted only for a BROAD signal, and a targeted row reaches its frames through `sourceMatches`.

`library.html:747` — "How a Fabricate record points at a game-world document. Three states in one component." 6 callers spread across the checks, component, essence, recipe-item and tool editors, which is why no single frame is the honest evidence.
`library.html:1104` and `:1137` name it and its two callers — the import folder-mapping step and the import report — and `:1137` records that ruling it out as single-caller was wrong.
`library.html:626` — "A radio group with room to explain itself." 9 callers.

The resolution-mode chooser card (2 callers, `CraftingSettingsView.svelte` and `GatheringEconomyView.svelte`). `library.html:1606` defers the modes themselves to the resolution-modes capability and specifies no card for choosing one. Targeted: `manager-system-edit-normal` claims it.
`library.html:1510` and `:1516` — cursor insertion and an actor resolver are behaviour nothing else owns, which is why it is a primitive where `<Bounds>` and `<Currency>` are compositions.

`library.html:764` — "One panel for picking anything from a catalogue". 20 callers over 24 call sites as issue 1458 lands, up from 16: three hand-rolled trigger-plus-listbox add menus (`GatheringEventEditView`, `GatheringTaskEditView`, `ModifierPillSelect`) and the recipe item editor’s Link-recipe menu converted onto it. That change also gave it the `triggerHasPopup` capability, which absorbs the one axis the ten hand-rolled popovers disagreed on — four announced `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and four `listbox`, and the split tracked whether the panel rendered a query field. Carries a THREE-entry `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry because it now has three deliberate presentations (inline-search trigger, value-bearing trigger with the search row, and the search-less option list) and neither representative frame opens a popover at all. Its class family is still the legacy World › Travel name `.manager-travel-*`, which this conversion knowingly concentrates rather than renames, so the rename that follows is a one-file edit plus the sheet. The SCOPING half of that sentence is withdrawn at issue 1472 and written out rather than deleted: it claimed 113 rules in that family and every one of them under `.fabricate-manager`, which was true of the sheet the plan was drafted against and false of the sheet it merged into — issue 1464 re-rooted the family thirteen minutes before the first row repeating it landed, and nothing re-measured. The family is 62 `.manager-travel-*` rules in `styles/fabricate.css`: 25 `.manager-travel-*` rules under `.fabricate-picker` in `styles/fabricate.css`, which are the primitive’s own on its own namespace root, and 37 `.manager-travel-*` rules under `.fabricate-manager` in `styles/fabricate.css`, which are the World › Travel SCREEN plus manager callers’ overrides of their own trigger sites. Those three figures are re-derived from the stylesheet by `tests/design-system-coverage.test.js` rather than asserted, which is exactly what the sentence they replace lacked. The scoping is therefore no longer a reason anything cannot convert, and the two PLAYER-app rows in {@link NOT_A_PRIMITIVE} no longer rest on it.
`library.html:613` — two to four named options, exactly one chosen, rendered as a radio group. 11 callers.

The subject-and-modifier picker (2 callers, `ComponentEditView.svelte` and `GatheringTaskEditView.svelte`). `library.html:1406` specifies `<RuleRow>` and `<RuleSentence>` as the condition editor behind "triggers, gates and modifiers", so this picker is specified as part of that editor rather than as an entry of its own. Targeted: one modifier-pick frame per caller claims it.

A titled card wrapping a binary control (7 callers). `<Toggle>` (`library.html:595`) is the bare control and `<Card>` (`:941`) is the container, so a card-plus-toggle is a COMPOSITION of two entries under spec.md requirement "The primitive set is a closed, versioned vocabulary" rather than an entry itself. Recorded here because it SHIPS with seven callers; whether the set should contain it is the conformance change's question.

The environment editor's composition list (issue 1321). `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/environment/EnvironmentTasksTab.svelte` and `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/environment/EnvironmentEventsTab.svelte` both import it, parameterised by `kind`, so it clears the two-caller bar. Its row claimed ONE caller and named `environment/EnvironmentCompositionTab.svelte` for it — a file that has never existed anywhere in this repository — and every gate passed on it. That is the finding issue 1446 was opened on, and the reason the non-member rows carry a MEASURED `callers` field now instead of a sentence. The two callers are sibling TABS of one editor, so "independent" is worth stating rather than assuming. Each renders the list against a different entity kind, a different composition model and a different set of menu verbs, so a change made for one is a change the other has to survive, which is what the bar protects. What they are not is two different SCREENS, and the reading applied here is the mechanical one this module states: an importer is any other file under `src/` that imports the component by path. That is the reading a guard can decide, and a bar decided by judgement alone is the bar this row was recorded against wrongly. `library: null`, and three entries were considered rather than one. `library.html:1049` heads `<ListRow> <BrowseCard> <ViewToggle> <XrefList>` and states that "every browse list in the app is this row"; this is measurably not that row, because it renders FOUR sections at once — Included, Available to add, Excluded and a paged Non-matching — each an independent `<ul>` with its own empty state, and its verbs move a row BETWEEN them. `<SetPicker>` (`library.html:1351`) is the entry for editing set membership and rules itself out in its own sentence: it "never dumps the whole set into the panel it sits in", and dumping the whole set into the panel is exactly what this does. `<SortableList>` (`library.html:1447`) requires "both affordances always", the grip AND the chevrons, and this offers drag alone and only in the ranked-event mode. Claiming any of the three would assert a shape the tree does not have, which is the `ManagerSearchField` call again. Its issue 1458 adjudication SURVIVES the move, because a component can be a member of the set and still carry a recorded non-conversion. Its four popovers (`:373`, `:553`, `:688`, `:827`) were adjudicated against `SearchablePopover` and ruled a different widget: each is `aria-haspopup="menu"` opening a `role="menu"` of `role="menuitem"` children — an ACTION menu — while the primitive renders `role="listbox"`/`role="option"`, a SELECTION control. Converting them would change what a screen reader announces from "menu, four items" to "listbox, four options, none selected", which is a claim about the widget rather than about its styling. It carries no `<style>` block at all, so its exposure to the scoped-rule failure was nil and the exclusion is about meaning alone. The group is still a legitimate candidate for a shared ACTION-menu primitive of its own — four sites in one file, and `ComponentIdentityStrip`'s source-actions overflow is a fifth site that went the other way and is a `SearchablePopover` today — but that is a different primitive from this one. Targeted, and no `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry is owed. All four cases that claim it do so through `^src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/environment/`, the same directory-anchored pattern that claims both callers, so every frame that renders either caller already publishes on a change here — `manager-environment-edit-blind-weights` and `manager-environment-edit-automatic-force-add` are named for two of this component's own controls. An override would be inert regardless: it is consulted only for a BROAD signal.
A single-value percentage slider (4 callers). `<RangeBar>` (`library.html:714`) specifies a TILED strip of spans whose dividers are dragged, which is `ThresholdBandStrip`, not this.

The category-group header of a grouped browser list (2 callers). `<ListRow>` (`library.html:1033`) specifies the ROW; the group header above a run of rows is not one of the four entries under that head.

The essence source picker (2 callers). `library.html:764` names essences among the catalogues its four existing pickers COLLAPSE INTO `<SearchPopover>`; this file is one of those pickers and is not that panel today, so recording the name would fill the conformant quadrant with work not done. Issue 1458 measured what the collapse costs and left it: the TRIGGER is a drop-target image tile with an empty state and a corner glyph, sitting beside a clear button inside a `dragDrop` shell, and `SearchablePopover` owns its trigger button outright — so the conversion needs a caller-owned trigger SNIPPET the primitive does not have. Its option list is a GRID of image tiles rather than a row list, its popover is bounded 280-420px against the primitive’s 240-340, and its empty message varies by whether the catalogue is empty or the query matched nothing. Four capabilities for one caller is a redesign, not a conversion.

THE manager's labelled form field, the `.manager-field` column (issue 1428). 81 callers across 23 components, second only to `ManagerButton` under `components/`. `library.html:646` heads its block `<Field> <Select> <Search>` and states that "the kicker label above the field is part of the primitive, not something each screen re-invents" — which is exactly the box this ships. The block's other two names stay in the specified-but-unbuilt register: the 38px control shell, the option list and the `value`/`onChange`/`options` API are not built, and this claims the entry at the same granularity `Chip` claims `<IconChip>` from a block that also names `<Kicker>` and `<StatBox>`. Carries a two-entry `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry because neither representative frame renders a `.manager-field` at all: `manager-components-normal` is a browse list and `fabricate-app-shell` is the player shell.

The product's one horizontal fill bar (2 callers). `library.html:872` splits the instrument into `<Meter>`, `<BandedBar>` and `<StageBars>` and states that merging them leaves one component unable to carry a correct accessible role, "which is why the shipped fill leaf renders none" — this is that leaf, so it corresponds to no single entry by the library's own account.

The manager's icon-only push-button (36 callers, issue 1422), extracted from 82 hand-rolled `class="manager-icon-button"` sites across 37 components. `library.html:570` heads one specimen `<Button> <IconButton>` and specifies the icon size on that ladder (`icon 28x28 - radius 7`) with `ariaLabel` REQUIRED when icon-only, which is the entry this row names. Two divergences from that specimen are deliberate and are recorded rather than smoothed over: the shipped control is 34px (`fabricate.css:13935`), 28px only inside `.manager-pagination`, so the ladder value and the shipped pixel disagree and this change does not repaint 82 sites to settle it; and it takes NO `role` prop, because its modifiers mix roles with states and one site compounds two, so the vocabulary is a design ruling left open rather than folded into a sweep whose acceptance bar is that no frame moves. Broad by reach rather than by count alone: it lands in nearly every studio, browser, inspector and editor tab, and through `Pagination` it reaches the player apps too.

The shared icon picker (8 callers, issue 1269). `library.html:764` names icons FIRST among the catalogues collapsing into `<SearchPopover>`; same reasoning as `EssenceSourceSelector`. Carries a `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry because everything it presents exists only in the open popover and neither representative frame opens one. Issue 1458 measured the collapse and left it: this picker needs FIVE capabilities the primitive lacks — a PINNED resolved row above an alphabetical list of ~1000 (without it the picker always opens on `abacus`), `horizontalAlign: iconOnly ? 'left' : 'right'` against the primitive’s hard-coded `left`, a measured `listMaxHeight` fed back into the layout, a `style` on the trigger for the colour swatch, and `oncontextmenu`/`onkeydown` pass-throughs the trigger’s own attribute set would override. Its rows also wrap the glyph in a `.essence-icon-picker-preview` tile the primitive renders bare, so the conversion changes what eight callers draw.

THE manager's card shell (19 callers, issue 1427), extracted from 80 hand-written `class="manager-inspector-card"` sections across 20 components — every one of them a `<section>`, measured by walking each component's Svelte AST, so it takes no polymorphism prop. `library.html:941` heads one specimen `<Card> <Well> <RowDisclosure>` and states "two container levels only; a card sits on the page, a well nests inside a card" — this is that card, and the entry was in the specified-but-unbuilt register until it shipped. Two divergences from that specimen are deliberate and recorded rather than smoothed over: the shipped box is radius 8 with `--fab-space-3` padding on `--fab-overlay-light-04` (`fabricate.css:13663`) against the specimen's radius 11 / padding 16 / bg-2, and the sheet declares three further treatments keyed on a modifier class (`.manager-checks-card`), on an ANCESTOR (`.manager-checks-rail`, which reaches cards carrying no modifier at all) and on a positioning state (`.is-sticky`, which — measured across `src/` — no component writes at all) — so it takes NO variant prop, because a vocabulary spanning three different anchors is a design ruling and not something to settle inside a sweep whose acceptance bar is that no frame moves. `<Well>`, the level below it, remains unbuilt. Broad by reach: the Checks Studio, both environment inspectors, the essence and tool inspectors, the books-and-scrolls inspector, the Tool Studio authority card and the shared bulk-delete card all render it, and the deferred root holds 32 more sites. It carries a `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry because NEITHER representative frame contains a card at all.

`library.html:570` — one component, six roles, two sizes, each role naming a VERB. The shipped `role` prop is that closed set, made required-shaped precisely because the CSS-convention version drifted. 50 callers, the most of anything under `components/`.

THE manager's search field (20 callers, issue 1039), extracted from 23 hand-written `class="manager-search"` labels — every one of them a `<label>` wrapping an `<i class="fas fa-search">` and an `<input type="search">`, measured by walking each component's Svelte AST, so it takes no polymorphism prop and no icon prop. `library:null` is a judgement, not an omission. `library.html:649` specifies `<Search>` as ONE OF THREE modes SHARING ONE SHELL with a kicker label above the field, at height 38 / radius 9. The shipped pill is not that shell: it is 34 / radius 6 (`fabricate.css:5730`), it carries no kicker and no label prop — its accessible name is an `aria-label` on the inner input at all 20 sites — and the manager's select mode is a separate treatment (`.manager-filter select`, `:5741`) this component does not touch, while the shell itself now ships as `Field.svelte` claiming `<Field>`. Recording the correspondence would assert that the shipped tree has the one shell the library specifies, which it measurably does not, so the entry stays in the specified-but-unbuilt register and the adjudication belongs to whichever change unifies the three modes. Same call, and the same reason, as `EditorValidationSurface`. Three of the 23 sites are ADJUDICATED OPT-OUTS rather than deferrals: `GatheringTaskEditView.svelte:1747` and both `CraftingSystemManagerRoot.svelte` sites render a `.manager-tag-suggestions` typeahead list inside the label, which makes them comboboxes belonging to `SearchablePopover`, and the root's two additionally take `bind:this` on the label for popover positioning — which on a COMPONENT tag binds the component instance, not its host element. Broad by reach: every browse screen plus four editors and three rosters. It carries a `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry because the representative pair reaches only the base density.

THE manager's filter bar (11 callers, issue 1039), extracted from 11 hand-written `class="manager-toolbar"` sections — every one of them a `<section>`, measured by walking each component's Svelte AST, so it takes no polymorphism prop. A raw grep says TWELVE and is wrong: `GatheringTaskEditView.svelte:1784` is a `.manager-toolbar-pills` chip row on a `<div>`, and `\b` matches before a hyphen. `library.html:1211` heads `<Pagination> <FilterBar>` and `spec.md`'s browse archetype names "the filter bar" as a fixed element of every browse screen; this is that bar, and the entry was in the specified-but-unbuilt register until it shipped. THREE divergences from the specimen are recorded rather than smoothed over. (1) The library's FilterBar API owns its controls as DATA — `query`, `toggles`, `selects`, `segments`, `sort`, `result`, `onClear` — and the shipped bar owns only the CHROME and takes its controls as children, because the corpus's filter control is three different things (a `<label class="manager-filter">` wrapping a `<select>`, 16 sites; a bare `<select>` carrying its own accessible name, 2; and `<SegmentedControl>`, 2) and no bar is in a position to choose between them. (2) The sketch specifies ONE component owning both bar and query, and the corpus has TWO: 13 of the 23 search fields render inside no bar at all, so a field folded into the bar would have forced a bar around each of them. The field ships as `ManagerSearchField.svelte`, recorded separately below. (3) It takes NO variant prop — the sheet declares four further treatments anchored four different ways, two of them scrolling caps (`.manager-environments-toolbar`, `.manager-task-toolbar`), one sized from a SCOPED rule in `scoped/EntityListInspectorFrame.svelte` rather than from the sheet at all, and one (`.manager-toolbar:not(:has(.manager-toolbar-primary))`) a branch that is ALWAYS taken because — measured across `src/` — no component writes `.manager-toolbar-primary`, so the grid form at `fabricate.css:5671` is declared and never rendered. Broad by reach: every browse screen in the manager renders it. It carries a `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry because the representative pair reaches only the base treatment.
`library.html:797`. 4 callers. The tint swatch panel; its sibling `ManagerColorPicker.svelte` is the single-caller trigger and is recorded in `NOT_A_PRIMITIVE`.

The flat identity tile for recipe rows and inspectors (13 callers). `<Avatar>` (`library.html:1225`) is a person mark in a rail; this renders a record's linked image with a glyph fallback, so the correspondence is not made.

A dropdown-plus-removable-pills multi-select (2 callers, issue 770). `<SetPicker>` (`library.html:1333`) specifies editing membership of a set too large to render inline, and states it never dumps the whole set into its panel — this control renders every unselected option in a listbox, so it is not that primitive. Its ADD MENU is `SearchablePopover` since issue 1458, which is why the pill row and the menu are now two different things rather than one hand-rolled widget; the conversion needed the primitive to absorb `triggerAriaDisabled`, the at-cap state that must refuse to open while staying focusable, because the post-removal focus fallback lands on that very button and `focus()` on a `disabled` one silently no-ops. It carries a `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry as of that change: `manager-recipe-edit-crafting-modifier-cap-reached` is the one frame that draws its single remaining painted rule, the at-cap trigger treatment.
Named at `library.html:1196`. 22 callers across every browse surface in the manager.
`library.html:689` — "The box a gate list and a selection header both use", including the tri-state a some-rows-selected header needs. 8 callers.

The row and inspector state pill, six tones (13 callers). The library's mark vocabulary (`library.html:835`, `:858`) specifies marks that carry KIND; this pill carries STATE, and `library.html:348` states that colouring a chip background by kind would double-code kind against state — so it is deliberately not one of those marks.

`library.html:595` — "Binary state that takes effect immediately", and the manager's one on/off switch (25 callers, issue 1040). It was a CSS convention over an element TREE — track span, nested knob span, optional reading — hand-written at 37 sites in 26 components, and `scoped/InheritRow.svelte` and `scoped/MembershipActions.svelte` each recorded in their own docblocks that they had to. Carries a three-entry `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry because its `as` prop is a closed set of three element HOSTS and no representative frame draws even one of them: `fabricate-app-shell` is the player window and `manager-components-normal` holds only the track-only filter switch. The shipped 34x20 track against this ladder's 38x22 is recorded as a migration in the entry's own delta, not resolved here.

`library.html:551` — "The most-used control in the app", and 23 callers here agree. Carries a `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry naming the gathering economy actor frame, which is the only published frame that renders filled steppers, disabled steppers and a rolled-max placeholder at once.

`library.html:714` — a tiled strip of spans whose dividers are dragged, "outcome tiers against a DC", which is exactly this. Exactly 2 callers, `checks/CraftingCheckEditor.svelte` and `checks/SimpleCraftingCheckEditor.svelte`, and it carries a two-entry `BROAD_SIGNAL_CASE_OVERRIDES` entry because those are its two modes and each renders chrome the other does not.

notAPrimitive.why: ADJUDICATED against `EditorValidationSurface` at issue 1444 and ruled a different surface AND a different kind of thing: a whole ROUTE, not a tab. Measured: `.manager-main manager-system-overview-main` (`:190`) with a `.manager-section-header`, a `.manager-chip-row` of `Chip` counts (`:209`) where the surface has a counts rail, and `.manager-system-overview-list` (`:259`) grouped by entity kind rather than by check category. It writes zero tokens of either family. One caller: `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/SystemEditView.svelte`.

ONE caller, `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/downtime/WorldDowntimeExtensionHost.svelte`. That caller count is what puts the row on THIS list, exactly as it does for the other nine, and the maintainer's divergence ruling does not touch it: one caller is below the two-caller bar however the file is drawn. What the ruling does touch is the second half of the row, the reasoning that told the next audit not to re-propose converting it onto `EditorTabs` — and issue 1429 re-read that reasoning and found it DOES NOT SURVIVE. It is recorded here as CONVERSION-PENDING, not as a justified divergence. Issue 1038's ground (1) was `177 lines of its own scoped <style> ... so the component owns a layout, not just a tablist`, and re-reading the block splits it three ways. `.downtime-tab-card`, `.downtime-connected-studio`, its `strong`/`p` and `.downtime-connected-icon` author a CARD and a sibling identity block that are not the tablist at all; a host that wrapped `<EditorTabs>` would keep every one of them, so they show that the FILE owns a layout and show nothing about the strip. `.downtime-tabs`, the bare `button` rule, its `:hover`/`:focus-visible`/`.is-active` re-tone and the `@container (max-width: 720px)` collapse draw the tablist and its buttons as bordered, filled, 8px-radius pills instead of the shared `.manager-editor-tab*` underline — which is a STYLE divergence, and spec.md requirement "Near-neighbour primitives are routed by a stated rule" states that a deliberate style divergence is precisely what a shared primitive exists to remove. Only the padlock (`.downtime-tab-lock` plus the currency re-tone) and the visible hover/focus tooltip are per-tab CONTENT and BEHAVIOUR the primitive has no vehicle or slot for, and those are the functional-or-informational kind the ruling admits. Ground (2), `activeTabId` rather than `activeTab` and no `badges`, is a RENAME and was never a divergence. Ground (3) is real and behavioural — `focusableTabId` falls back to the first tab when `activeTabId` names no rendered tab, so the strip keeps a tab stop while `aria-selected` stays bound to `activeTabId` — but the ruling admits a functional difference as something the primitive ABSORBS AS A CAPABILITY, and `EditorTabs` binding `tabindex` to `activeTab === tab.id` means any strip whose active id names no rendered tab loses its tab stop entirely. That is a defect in the primitive, not a licence for a second strip. So conversion is owed, and issue 1429 deliberately did not attempt it: it needs four capabilities on `EditorTabs` (a per-tab lock affordance, a per-tab accessible-name override, a visible tooltip carrying `aria-describedby` with its own hover/focus state, and the focus fallback) plus hoisting roughly a hundred lines of scoped button and container-query CSS into shipped `styles/fabricate.css` classes, because a scoped rule left on the caller would match nothing once the button is rendered by a child. That is a larger change than the conversion it would accompany and it touches a shared stylesheet, so it is follow-up work rather than a silent extension. Targeted: the `manager-world-downtime-*` frames render it and claim it by `sourceMatches`.

ADJUDICATED against `EditorValidationSurface` at issue 1444 and ruled a DIFFERENT SURFACE rather than an unconverted one, so the next audit does not re-propose it. Measured: it renders `.manager-environment-card`, `.manager-environment-check-list` and `.manager-environment-issue-list`, carries no status medallion, no counts rail and no grouped row stack, and expresses severity through `Chip` (`:140`) rather than a `manager-recipe-val-pill`. It writes zero `manager-recipe-val-*` and zero `manager-recipe-rail-*` tokens, and each of its three classes appears in exactly one file. Converting it would be a visual REDESIGN of the environment editor, not an adoption. One caller: `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/EnvironmentEditView.svelte`.

ONE caller, `src/ui/svelte/apps/FabricateAppRoot.svelte`. This is an UNADJUDICATED SCREEN REGION and not a candidate that cannot work as a primitive, and as of issue 1472 that is the whole of the row: at 594 lines it is a screen region rather than a primitive, and `<AppTitleBar>` (`library.html:965`) specifies the strip above the page header and nav rail, but whether this bar implements that entry has never been decided. Both are open questions rather than objections, so a re-proposal here is answered by adjudicating the correspondence — a design ruling, not a measurement. The row’s SECOND reason, a structural non-conversion recorded against its actor picker at issue 1458, is WITHDRAWN, and is written out rather than deleted because a row that quietly loses an argument is how this register drifted in the first place. It said the picker renders in the PLAYER window under `.fabricate-app-shell` while all 113 rules in the `.manager-travel-*` family were scoped under `.fabricate-manager`, so converting it would portal to a host that is not there and render the panel entirely unstyled. Neither half survives. Issue 1466 replaced the hard-coded `closest()` on `.fabricate-manager` with `resolveOverlayHost`, whose root set carries `fabricate-app`, and `tests/components/overlay-portal-host-position.test.js` measures a `SearchablePopover` landing at its trigger inside the player window. Issue 1464 re-rooted the primitive’s own family at `.fabricate-picker`, so the 37 `.manager-travel-*` rules under `.fabricate-manager` in `styles/fabricate.css` that remain are the World › Travel screen plus manager callers’ overrides; four of those DO name a class the primitive writes, and all four are anchored on a manager-only container — `.manager-salvage-component-trigger`, `.manager-tool-replacement-card`, `.manager-map-link-picker-cell`, `.manager-recipe-or-popover` — that the player window never renders. The picker itself measures as a single-select searchable popover: one `role="listbox"`, `aria-selected` on `store.selectedActorId` alone, a query field and close-on-choose. So nothing recorded here blocks its conversion any more, and converting it is deliberately NOT done at issue 1472, which corrected the record and changed no markup: this row judges the BAR, and the picker inside it is a change of its own.

ZERO callers — dead code. Nothing under `src/` imports it. (`src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/ItemDropZone.svelte` is a DIFFERENT FILE: it is the shipped link field and a member of the set. A basename search that does not anchor on the path separator conflates the two and credits this dead component with every one of that file’s importers, which is why `scripts/lib/componentImporters.js` resolves each specifier against the directory that wrote it, compares whole repository-relative paths, and never compares a basename at all.)

ZERO callers — dead code, and the one row where the library and the tree disagree in the interesting direction: `library.html:797` specifies `<ArtPathPicker>`, and a file implementing it ships, and nothing imports it. Specified and built is not the same as shipped.

ONE caller, `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/EnvironmentsBrowserView.svelte`. The `<TintPicker>` entry is carried by its sibling `ManagerColorPopover.svelte`, which clears the bar and is a member of the set.

ONE caller, `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/ComplicationSummaryRow.svelte`. Named at `library.html:941`, so it is specified and shipped and still below the entry bar. It is separately on `SHARED_PRIMITIVES` in `tests/components/mounted-harness-primitive-allowlist.test.js:83` for a reason the caller count cannot express — omitting it there HANGS a mounted tree — which is why that list is not derived from this manifest.

ONE caller, `src/ui/svelte/apps/manager/RecipeItemEditor.svelte`, and it is a route tab rather than a candidate primitive. The caller recorded here until issue 1446 was `recipe-item/RecipeItemEditorTabs.svelte`, a real sibling that imports `EditorTabs` and does not import this tab at all: the COUNT was right and the FILE was wrong, which is the half of the drift a count check on its own cannot see. It is recorded because issue 1458 adjudicated the two `role="listbox"` SITES inside it (`:531`, `:631`) against `SearchablePopover` and ruled them a DIFFERENT WIDGET, which is a decision a later audit would otherwise re-propose from the same grep. They are typeahead COMBOBOXES: neither has a trigger button at all, the suggestion list hangs off an `<input>` whose `aria-expanded={suggestions.length > 0}` (`:537`, `:637`) is driven by the query rather than by a control, and the input IS the field rather than a filter over a panel. `SearchablePopover` opens a panel FROM a trigger; a combobox has no closed state to open from. `manager-filter-bar-source-contract.test.js` already records the same verdict for the three `.manager-search` comboboxes, from the other side. The file carries 30 scoped rules and a silent-mode trigger (`<i class={expr}>`), so a conversion would have been the highest-risk one in the candidate set as well as the wrongest.

ONE caller, `src/ui/svelte/components/ActorSelectTopBar.svelte`. Recorded because issue 1458 adjudicated its editor popover (`:134`, `:138`) against `SearchablePopover` and found TWO independent disqualifiers, either of which is sufficient. (1) IS WITHDRAWN at issue 1472, and is written out rather than deleted because a row that quietly loses an argument is how this register drifted: it said the panel renders in the PLAYER window under `.fabricate-app-shell` while all 113 rules in the `.manager-travel-*` family were scoped under `.fabricate-manager`, so it would portal to a host that is not there and draw completely unstyled. Issue 1466 put `fabricate-app` into `resolveOverlayHost`’s root set and issue 1464 re-rooted the primitive’s family at `.fabricate-picker`; the `components/ActorSelectTopBar` row carries the measurement. (2) STANDS ENTIRELY ON ITS OWN, and is why this row is still here. It is a MULTI-SELECT checklist rather than a picker: `toggleAvailable` toggles membership, the popover stays open across choices, and `aria-selected` is true on every chosen actor at once, while `SearchablePopover` has a single `value` and closes on `choose`. It also has NO search field at all — the file renders no `<input>` — against a primitive whose panel is built around one. Converting it would take four clicks to add four source actors and would tell assistive technology that one option is selected when four are, so a conversion needs a multi-select mode on the primitive, which is a design question this row does not settle. Its 28 scoped rules carry NO silent-mode trigger — measured, against the file’s own AST — so they would have pruned and warned rather than dying quietly; that is the one at-risk file in the candidate set where the recorded silencing condition does not hold.

ruledOut.name: <MemberRow>
ruledOut.why: List row geometry with a portrait in the leading cell — structurally identical to the inline-title row already declined.

ruledOut.name: <ActorPicker>
ruledOut.why: A pill trigger that opens the popover — which already counted it as one of its four callers.

ruledOut.name: <AddButton>
ruledOut.why: Dashed is a role on the button that owns the meaning. "Sits in flow with its collection" is a usage rule, not a boundary.

ruledOut.name: <RailCard>
ruledOut.why: A composition that also smuggled back the 34px button size the set retires by name.

ruledOut.name: <FeatureCard>
ruledOut.why: Two ABSENT props on an identical shape is a props difference, not a distinction.

ruledOut.name: <BoundsInput>
ruledOut.why: "Two steppers with a rule between", by its own spec.

ruledOut.name: <CurrencyInput>
ruledOut.why: A composition, and wrong about the domain: it assumed a flat world-scoped coin ladder where the model defines a per-system acyclic denomination DAG.

ruledOut.name: <PremiumPanel>
ruledOut.why: A screen, not a primitive. Its one original claim is copy — a product decision — and binding copy to a component makes the offer untranslatable against a codebase where every primitive takes pre-localized strings. Canon also forbids any premium signal in the player window.

ruledOut.name: <Toast>
ruledOut.why: Foundry owns transient feedback and renders its own toasts over the module window regardless.

ruledOut.name: Destructive panel
ruledOut.why: Canon makes the dialog the default for manager confirmations; the arm is the carve-out.
